results.title: Agent Managers for Mac: Desktop Apps for AI Coding
results.content:
It depends on how you work. If you only use Claude Code and only use a Mac, Conductor and Superset are polished Mac-first apps. If you switch between agents like Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, or also work on Windows or Linux, Pane runs any CLI agent and works the same on all three. If you'd rather stay in a terminal, Herdr and Claude Squad are good fits.
 Pane, Orca, T3 Code, Emdash, Conductor, Traycer, Reliant, Kandev, super.engineering and Agentastic ship Intel builds. Ghostex, Waku and HumanLayer's desktop app are Apple Silicon only, and bb's Mac app is Apple Silicon only, with npx on Intel.
 No. Pane ships a signed, notarized DMG for Apple Silicon and one for Intel. Drag it to Applications and open it. Claude Squad and some other terminal tools use Homebrew, and they need tmux. [...] Conductor and Superset both ask you to sign in to their own account before you start. Conductor is closed source, with paid cloud and team plans. Pane and Paseo open straight to work with no account, as do the terminal tools. Orca and T3 Code only ask for one when you pair a phone, and Emdash opens on a screen asking you to connect GitHub. You still sign in to the agent CLIs themselves, like Claude Code or Codex.

## Which to pick

Pick by how many agents you use and whether you ever leave the Mac. [...] On a Mac, the choice is about workflow, not compatibility.

Mac-first apps such as Conductor, Superset, cmux, super.engineering and Agentastic are built around macOS. Some are native Swift apps and feel at home there. The trade-off is that your setup stays on the Mac, and if your team also uses Windows or Linux, they can't share it.

Cross-platform desktop apps such as Pane, Orca, T3 Code, Paseo and Emdash give each agent its own git worktree, a diff viewer and git buttons, and work the same on all three systems.

Terminal tools such as Herdr, Claude Squad and Sidecar run inside your terminal. They're light and work over SSH, but you read changes as text and manage panes with keyboard shortcuts.
